newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand denies seeking finance merger.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand denies seeking finance merger.

text.p: Thailand's central bank on Monday denied newspaper reports that it plans to force immediate mergers among 30 troubled finance companies to limit damage to the ailing finance sector.

"The Bank of Thailand wishes to refute the recent reports in several newspapers that the bank had proposed to the government to issue a special decree to force 30 finance companies to merge," it said in a statement received on Monday.

Local media carried reports on Sunday quoting unidentified sources as saying forced mergers were being planned and that the central bank would seek a decree from the cabinet giving it absolute authority to tackle the ailing finance sector.
Newspapers had said the decree, apparently sought by the central bank, would have empowered it to order finance companies to merge without having to seek shareholder approval.

However, the central bank said it proposed to the Ministry of Finance that it issue an announcement setting new details and conditions that finance companies may merge and apply for banking licences or additional retail banking businesses.

"The pending announcement will specify the qualifications of the companies that will act as leaders in the friendly mergers. Interested companies can form themselves into groups and submit their applications right now instead of having to wait until December 1997 as set previously," the statement said.

The central bank statement comes over a week after the failed merger between ailing Finance One Plc and Thai Danu Bank Plc. The merger had the blessings of the authorities and was seen as a trend-setter for consolidations in the troubled Thai financial sector.
The two institutions cited tax and legal complications as reasons for the collapse of the merger.
The central bank has encouraged mergers to strengthen the financial sector in a bid to avert any potential financial meltdown.
